briefing_gaps_closed: The briefing's evidence.missing_sections listed DECOMPILATION, DISASSEMBLY, ABI and 'no persisted or live decompilation for this target'. All four were gathered live from the Ghidra bridge during this run: a 25-instruction disassembly, a decompilation, the Ghidra function record, and two raw vtable images. Nothing in this sidecar comes from a section the briefing left empty.

The briefing carried empty callers, callees, xrefs, globals, types, fields_offsets, semantic_findings and abi. The callee set here is machine-derived from three indirect dispatches in the listing plus the two vtable images, not from a call-graph export.

conclusions: Slot +0x34 holds 0x006a14d0 in BOTH images, so this is one function shared by two classes, not two same-named functions.
Slot +0x38 agrees in both images (0x006a1510), so the add step is not overridden between the two classes.

Slot +0x48 DISAGREES (0x006a2a80 vs 0x006a2b20), so the clear step IS overridden and the body is genuinely polymorphic. Both targets were decompiled live: 0x006a2a80 carries the Ghidra name App::PropertyList::Clear and 0x006a2b20 carries App::DirectPropertyList::Clear.

mechanics.guard: if (receiver == other) return; -- 0x006a14d8 CMP ESI,EDI with 0x006a14da JZ 0x006a1504. Pointer identity only: no alias, offset or range test appears anywhere in the body. A self-copy dispatches nothing at all -- no parent release, no clear, no add.
mechanics.parent_read: OpaquePropertyList *parent = receiver->word_030; -- 0x006a14dc MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x30]. This is the body's only field read, and the value lands in ECX, which is what makes the following release a call ON THE PARENT.
mechanics.parent_null_test: TEST ECX,ECX / JZ 0x006a14f1 at 0x006a14df/0x006a14e1 -- the jump target 0x006a14f1 is the Clear dispatch, so a null parent skips the store AND the release together, and the receiver's word at +0x30 is left as it was (already zero).
mechanics.parent_detach: receiver->word_030 = 0; -- 0x006a14e3 MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x30],0x0, executed BEFORE the release. The ordering is load-bearing and is preserved in the source: a re-entrant release that inspected the child through this word would observe it already cleared.

dispatch_1_release.target_semantics: 0x00432b50 is named FUN_00432b50 by Ghidra. Its own live decompilation reads the dword at param+0x04, decrements it by 2 under LOCK/UNLOCK, resets it to 2 and dispatches vtable slot +0x08 with argument 1 when it reaches zero, and on a new value of 3 calls through the pointer at param+0x14. That is a reference-count release; the -2 step and the param+0x14 callback are recorded here as observed behaviour of the CALLEE, not as an established layout of this class.

mechanics.vtable_is_read_twice: The receiver's vtable word is read at 0x006a14f1 (for slot +0x48) and again at 0x006a14fa (for slot +0x38) -- the second read is AFTER the clear has returned. The add target is therefore whatever slot +0x38 holds at that later moment, not what it held on entry. This is reproduced in the source as two separate reads and is exercised by model test case 4, where a clear that rebinds the vtable retargets the subsequent add.
mechanics.dispatch_order: release (0x006a14ef) -> clear (0x006a14f8) -> add (0x006a1502), fixed and unconditional on every non-self-copy path.

mechanics.globals: none. The 25-instruction listing names no data-segment address; the body reaches memory only through the receiver, the parent and the vtable images.
mechanics.indirect_transfers: three, all of the form MOV EDX,[EAX + slot] / CALL EDX at 0x006a14ef, 0x006a14f8 and 0x006a1502. No register-indirect or memory-indirect transfer of any other form appears.
mechanics.direct_transfers: none. There is no CALL or JMP with an immediate operand anywhere in the body, so this target has no statically-named callee -- consistent with the briefing's empty callees list, which is a property of the code and not a gap in the evidence.
mechanics.null_behavior: partial and explicit. A null `other` is NOT tested: it would be forwarded to the slot +0x38 target unchecked. A null parent IS tested, at 0x006a14df, and takes the skip arm. A null receiver is impossible under thiscall.
mechanics.aliasing: only exact self-identity is excluded. Overlapping-but-distinct receiver and argument, or a receiver sharing storage with its own parent, are not excluded by the body; whether those are safe is decided by the three callees.

return_semantics.basis: no path in the 25-instruction listing writes EAX with a return value, and the epilogue at 0x006a1504..0x006a1506 does not touch EAX. EAX's final writes are the vtable reads at 0x006a14f1/0x006a14fa, the slot fetches, and dead callee results. The live Ghidra prototype is also void.
return_semantics.ownership: The body performs a release through the parent's vtable but no acquisition, publication or teardown of its own, and it mutates exactly one receiver word (+0x30, to zero). It returns nothing.

unresolved_questions: Why the parent is detached before being released. The body stores zero at receiver+0x30 and only then dispatches the release on the parent, which reads like a deliberate unlink-then-release to break a cycle or to satisfy a re-entrancy invariant in 0x00432b50. Nothing in this body states the reason, and 0x00432b50's own body shows no path that reads the child's +0x30 word, so the ordering is observable but its motivation is not established here.

Whether the add step can see a stale view of the source. Slot +0x38 target 0x006a1510 dispatches slot +0x38 again on the receiver when the SOURCE has a parent (its own live decompilation reads argument+0x30 and, if non-null, recurses through its own slot +0x38 before calling slot +0x30). This body has just cleared the RECEIVER, and the source is a different object, so the interaction is presumably benign -- but this body performs no check that would make it so, and the recursion inside 0x006a1510 is not characterised here.

What receiver+0x30 actually holds. Ghidra's imported SDK structure names it mpParent, and the dispatch at 0x006a14ea treats it as an object with its own vtable (it is used as a thiscall receiver), which is strong evidence it is an object pointer. The binary carries no MSVC RTTI, so the name is decompiler-derived from the imported SporeGhidra_march2017 symbols and is not independently confirmed here.

Why slot +0x48 is overridden but slot +0x38 is not. The two vtable images share this body at +0x34 and 0x006a1510 at +0x38, yet carry different Clear implementations at +0x48. Whether the add step was deliberately left non-virtual (because it must behave identically for both list kinds) or was simply not needed as an override is not decidable from the vtable images alone.

Whether 0x00432b50 is the correct slot +0x04 target for BOTH classes at runtime. The two images agree on 0x00432b50 in that slot, which is as strong as static evidence gets, but the release is dispatched on the PARENT, whose dynamic type may be a third class not represented by either image.

Return-type evidence. Unlike the pkg-app-proplist-wave13 sibling, no machine-derived ABI record for this target was available to contradict void, so RETURN SEMANTICS has no known conflict. That is an absence of counter-evidence, not positive confirmation; the positive basis is the listing and the Ghidra prototype.

No evidence pack. reconstruction/evidence/006a14d0/evidence.json does not exist, so the reconstruction's facts are cited by live address rather than by a persisted artefact. An integrator may want to generate one before promotion.
